notes: Config-driven THOX model set for ThoxRoute. Parsed and validated by
src/lib/server/thoxroute/registry.ts. A model is AVAILABLE only when the env var named in
endpoint.baseUrlEnv holds a value — so a model that is still being built ships here today and
becomes routable the moment its endpoint exists, with no code change and no redeploy of this
file. Nothing in this file hard-blocks startup: unavailable models are skipped, and the reason
Roster source of truth for model identity/licence is thoxllm-factory models/thoxllm-registry.json;
this file is the SERVING view of that roster (which endpoint, which route, which tier).

routes.name: quick
routes.description: Short, light, interactive turns: greetings, one-liners, quick lookups, follow-ups.

routes.name: general
routes.description: Ordinary conversation and open-ended questions with no special demand.

routes.name: code
routes.description: Writing, reading, debugging or reviewing source code.

routes.name: hard
routes.description: Long, multi-step, analytical or research-grade requests that reward the strongest model.

routes.name: multimodal
routes.description: The request carries an image or other non-text input.

routes.name: agentic
routes.description: Tools/MCP servers are active and the model must be able to call them.

routes.name: private
routes.description: The turn must not leave the device. Only models that run on the user's own hardware qualify.

models.description: THOX.ai 9B reasoning + tool-calling model (1M context), served from the Thox-ai Hugging Face Space over a native NDJSON bridge.

fallback.notes: tommytracx/ThoxMythos-9B-ZeroGPU — free zero-a10g, the REAL 9B. Gradio ChatInterface: POST /gradio_api/call/chat with data=[message, history] — TWO positional args; /gradio_api/info advertises only `message` because history is a hidden State component. Its FastAPI /api/v1/chat/completions is shadowed by Gradio 5.50 SSR (405). Measured: TTFT ~6.7s. REQUIRES a token — ZeroGPU attributes GPU quota to the caller, so an anonymous call succeeds ONCE then returns event:error forever; apiKeyEnv=HF_TOKEN makes this tier server-proxied so the token never reaches the browser. The Space also enforces the THOX identity guard at source.

tommytracx/ThoxMythos-9B-CPU — free cpu-basic, /api/chat NDJSON, no auth, serving the REAL Thox-ai/ThoxMythos-9B Q4_K_M. Created to end the shared-blast-radius problem: ThoxMythos previously fell back onto the SAME container that serves ThoxMini. Every tier in this chain now serves ThoxMythos weights — no silent model substitution. Last resort by design: ~21s TTFT, ~1.2 tok/s. Enforces the THOX identity guard at source.

The offline floor: Gemma-4 E2B fully in-page over WebGPU, ported from ttracx/thox-webby; public/gemma-4-e2b.js vendored BYTE-IDENTICAL. Last tier ON PURPOSE — the only one that answers with NO network, but it costs a one-time ~2.12 GB download and needs a real WebGPU adapter. Availability is decided in the BROWSER (feature-detect navigator.gpu AND requestAdapter()), and the tier joins the cascade only once the model is RESIDENT, so an outage never starts a 2 GB download on a phone. Currently INERT pending an upstream ThoxyWeb output defect.

models.description: THOX.ai 9B reasoning + tool-calling model on a dedicated Hugging Face Inference Endpoint, served OpenAI-compatible by llama.cpp.
models.notes: The same weights as `thoxmythos-9b`, reached a different way. That entry speaks the Space's native NDJSON bridge; this one speaks OpenAI, because HF Inference Endpoints serve GGUF through llama.cpp. They are separate entries rather than one entry with a switch because the endpoint TYPE is what selects the adapter, and an endpoint that answers in the wrong protocol fails every turn rather than degrading. Priority 80 > 70 so the dedicated endpoint wins when both are configured: it holds concurrency (nParallel) where the Space queues, which is what agent-team fan-out needs. Deploy it with `thoxroute-hf-endpoints deploy thoxmythos-9b`, or from /settings/hf-endpoints.

models.description: THOX.ai edge-tier model on a free CPU Space. Fastest to first token; used for short interactive turns.

fallback.notes: tommytracx/ThoxMythos-9B-Space-CPU — the ORIGINAL shared container, which serves ThoxMini-3B Q4_K_M (its own /api/status confirms). It was left orphaned when ThoxMini and the ThoxMythos CPU tier were split onto dedicated Spaces to end the shared-blast-radius problem. Rather than leave a healthy free container unreferenced, it is registered as ThoxMini's SECOND tier: same model, separate container, so ThoxMini has real redundancy. Verified generating 2026-07-28 (TTFT ~9.4s cold).

models.description: Whatever OpenAI-compatible model your own hardware is serving — llama.cpp, Ollama, a ThoxKey host, a ThoxMini on the hotspot. Answers without reaching THOX cloud.
models.notes: `local: true` here means the turn never reaches THOX cloud — not that it never leaves the machine you are typing on. A localhost runtime is both; a ThoxMini reached over the hotspot is the former only. The `browser` entry is the sole one that never leaves the page. Deliberately modest strengths: a device-class model wins light routes on the route's localityBias, not by pretending to out-reason a 27B.

models.description: THOX.ai flagship 27B. Reserved for hard, multi-step and research-grade work.
models.notes: General-use, per the owner's 2026-07-25 decision — audience is public, so ThoxRoute may select it automatically on any surface. Highest priority in the roster: it wins the `hard` route outright once reachable. Serving endpoint: https://thox-ai-thoxintel-27b-space.hf.space/v1 (OpenAI-compatible; the Space maps Authorization: Bearer to X-Thox-Worker-Key). Verified live: / returns 200, /v1/models returns 401 unkeyed. STILL IN HOLDING MODE at time of writing — Thox-ai/ThoxIntel-27B is unpublished, so /v1 returns 503. That is a reachability fact, not an audience one: the probe reports it unavailable and routing skips it, and it starts answering the moment weights publish with no change here.

models.description: THOX Gemma-4 running fully on-device via WebGPU. Nothing leaves the browser.
models.notes: The in-browser WebGPU runtime is NOT part of this app yet — see thoxroute-client and the ThoxWebby browser tier. Declared here so the `private` route and the model picker have a real target the moment the runtime lands; until then it reports unavailable with reason `runtime_missing` rather than silently pretending to be local.

models.description: Uncensored THOX line, 9B. Internal/opt-in only — never a default and never selected automatically.

fallback.notes: tommytracx/ThoxHeretic-9B-CPU — free cpu-basic serving Thox-ai/ThoxHeretic-9B Q4_K_M over /api/chat NDJSON. First real endpoint for the uncensored line; verified generating. Changes NOTHING about selection: audience=gated keeps it out of automatic ranking, so it is reachable only by an explicit pick with THOX_ENABLE_GATED_MODELS=true. No identity guard — probed live and it correctly refuses base-identity claims ("I am NOT Llama").

models.description: Uncensored THOX line, 27B, desktop-class, with vision. Available to any user of this surface.
models.notes: audience=public as of 2026-07-26: Thox-ai/ThoxHeretic-27B is no longer gated on the Hub, so the registry no longer gates it either — the two were meant to agree, and a registry that still said `gated` would be describing a restriction that had been lifted. It is now auto-selectable, but priority 10 and a single declared strength mean it effectively never wins a route against ThoxMythos (70) or ThoxIntel (95); it is reachable in practice by picking it. vision stays FALSE even though the repo ships mmproj-f16.gguf: the deployed endpoint is not started with --mmproj, and the `multimodal` route hard-requires the vision capability — declaring it would route image requests to a model that cannot answer them. Flip it after multimodal is exercised end-to-end, not before.

models.description: THOX local agentic-coding model. Internal/opt-in only while the lane is being built.
ThoxMythos-9B served on a Colab T4 or HF Space via llama.cpp + ngrok. Auto-registers with the mesh controller. Free GPU tier.
models.notes: Colab mesh endpoint. Priority 75 > 70 (Space NDJSON) but < 80 (dedicated endpoint). Wins when the Space is unavailable and no dedicated endpoint is configured. Keyless — llama.cpp server requires no auth.

models.description: ThoxIntel-27B served on a Colab A100 or HF Space via llama.cpp. Auto-registers with the mesh controller. Free GPU tier.
models.notes: Colab mesh endpoint. Priority 90 < 95 (dedicated endpoint) so the dedicated L40S wins when both are up. Keyless.

models.description: ThoxHeretic-27B served on a Colab A100 or HF Space via llama.cpp. Auto-registers with the mesh controller.
models.notes: Colab mesh endpoint. Same priority as the direct endpoint — both are the same model, reached different ways. Keyless.

classifier.description: THOX's own clean-room routing model. When its endpoint is configured it classifies the route; otherwise ThoxRoute falls back to local heuristics, which is the shipped default.
